title: Three sessions, four snags
scenario:
A developer, Lin, ran three coding-agent sessions on one repo yesterday: two in Claude Code and one in the Codex app. Each hit a snag. You read Lin's notes.

Use the exhibit. Lin, the repo and the notes are made up for this case. Commands and behaviour are from the vendors' pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
LIN'S NOTES (made up)

A. 09:10  claude -w search-api
          Tests fail: config/secrets.json not found.
          It is in my main folder, listed in .gitignore.

B. 10:30  Codex app, Worktree chat. I pressed "Create
          branch here" and named it feature/search.
          On my laptop's main folder:
            git checkout feature/search
            fatal: 'feature/search' is already used by
            worktree at '...'

C. 13:00  Claude ran: rm docs/old-api.md
          I ran /rewind to before that prompt and picked
          "Restore code". docs/old-api.md is still gone.

D. 16:45  I made 3 commits on feature/ui this morning and
          did not push them. Then:
            claude --cloud "Finish the settings page"
          The cloud session has none of my 3 commits.

questions.prompt: Note A: why is config/secrets.json missing in the new worktree?

options.text: Gitignored files aren't copied; list it in .worktreeinclude
options.explanation: Right. A worktree is a fresh checkout. .worktreeinclude copies gitignored files that match its patterns.

options.text: Set worktree.baseRef to head so ignored files come along
options.explanation: "head" starts the worktree from your local commits. It does not copy gitignored files.

options.text: Worktrees run only with -p; start the session that way
options.explanation: Interactive worktree sessions work too. The file was never copied.

options.text: The worktree reads the main folder's files; restart it
options.explanation: A worktree has its own files. Ignored files are not there unless you copy them.

questions.prompt: Note B: why does the checkout fail on Lin's main folder?

options.text: The worktree is in detached HEAD, so the branch was never made
options.explanation: Lin made the branch with Create branch here. The error says the worktree already uses it.

options.text: A branch can be checked out in one place only; use Hand off
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI: Git only allows a branch to be checked out in one place at a time. Hand off moves the chat and code to Local.

options.text: Codex locks every branch it creates until the chat is archived
options.explanation: No page says that. Git itself refuses a second checkout of the same branch.

options.text: Branches made in a worktree can't be used outside of Codex
options.explanation: OpenAI says you can commit, push and open a pull request from that branch.

questions.prompt: Note C: why didn't Restore code bring docs/old-api.md back?

options.text: Restore code returns the conversation only, never any files
options.explanation: Restore code reverts file changes. The problem is how this file was deleted.

options.text: Checkpoints are off until Lin turns them on in settings.json
options.explanation: That is Gemini CLI. Claude Code saves a checkpoint before each prompt by itself.

options.text: Checkpoints skip changes made by Bash commands; use git
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: checkpointing does not track files modified by Bash commands, such as rm. Git history is the way back.

options.text: The file lived in another worktree, which a rewind can't see
options.explanation: The note shows the rm ran in this session. The rm itself is the problem.

questions.prompt: Note D: why does the cloud session lack Lin's 3 commits?

options.text: Cloud sessions start from an empty repo; Lin must attach files
options.explanation: The cloud session clones the repo from GitHub. It just can't see unpushed commits.

options.text: Lin should run claude --teleport to send the commits up first
options.explanation: --teleport pulls a cloud session back to the terminal. It does not send local commits.

options.text: Cloud sessions use the default branch only; merge into main
options.explanation: The cloud VM clones the current branch. It is the unpushed commits that are missing.

options.text: --cloud clones the remote branch, not the laptop; push first
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: the cloud VM clones your GitHub remote at your current branch, not your local checkout, so push first.
